description: I'm a student from Bangladesh and I'm taking part in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge all by myself. My project is about creating a storybook with pictures that tells the stories of old space machines that were left behind on the Moon and Mars, like the ones from the Opportunity, Pathfinder, and Apollo missions. I'm using real data from NASA to make it happen. Right now, I'm working on this project alone and I don't need any help from others.
summary:
'SPACE RELICS' is a documentary-style visual project that explores the legacy of NASA’s space exploration through the missions, machines, and scientific discoveries left behind on the Moon and Mars.

The project takes audiences through the Apollo missions and the journeys of Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity, with supporting coverage of the Phoenix lander and later Mars exploration. Using authentic NASA photographs, mission archives, historical records, and scientific findings, it explains how these spacecraft explored other worlds, what they discovered, the challenges they faced, and why their missions still matter.

SPACE RELICS addresses the challenge by transforming complex space-mission information into an engaging, accessible visual guide. Its documentary-style storytelling, clear explanations, mission timelines, and credited images help students and space enthusiasts understand the technology and science behind space exploration.

The project is important because it preserves the stories of past missions, encourages STEM learning, and inspires curiosity about the universe. It shows that even when a mission ends, its discoveries and engineering achievements continue to support future exploration.
details:
SPACE RELICS

SPACE RELICS is a documentary-style space science storytelling project that brings the remarkable journey of NASA’s Mars rover Opportunity to life. It presents the mission through a first-person, diary-inspired narrative, allowing audiences to follow the rover’s journey from its launch and landing to its discoveries, challenges, and final communication.

The project explains how NASA’s twin rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, were designed to investigate the Martian surface and search for geological evidence of past water. Through real NASA mission photographs and scientific findings, it highlights important discoveries such as the iron-rich hematite concretions known as “Martian blueberries,” the layered rocks of Eagle Crater, and the challenges Opportunity faced while exploring the planet. It also introduces the Phoenix Mars Lander as a separate supporting mission to provide additional context about water ice and the Martian environment.

The project works as a visual educational journey. Each section combines historical mission information, authentic space imagery, short explanations, and storytelling to make complex scientific topics easier to understand. The diary-inspired narration is based on documented mission events and data; it does not present fictional dialogue as an actual rover transmission.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The main benefit of SPACE RELICS is making Mars exploration and planetary science more accessible and interesting, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. It helps audiences understand how scientists use rocks, minerals, soil, and environmental observations to investigate the history of another planet. It also demonstrates the importance of scientific research, engineering, patience, problem-solving, and space exploration.

Our intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space, encourage STEM learning, and help people appreciate the scientific value of robotic missions. Most importantly, the project shows how a mission designed to last only 90 Martian days (sols) continued operating for 5,111 sols and travelled approximately 45.16 kilometres, far exceeding its original planned lifetime.

Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using Canva for presentation design, visual storytelling, image arrangement, and layout. A web browser was used to research mission history and access publicly available NASA/JPL scientific information and imagery. The project uses authentic mission photographs and documented findings as its primary visual and informational sources. No custom hardware or programming language was required; the work focused on research, science communication, and digital presentation design.

Creativity and Key Considerations

The creative approach is to tell a scientific story through the perspective of a robotic explorer. Instead of presenting only dates and technical facts, SPACE RELICS connects discoveries, engineering challenges, and mission milestones into a documentary-style narrative. The visual design aims to create an immersive Mars exploration experience while keeping the information clear and understandable.

During development, we considered scientific accuracy, reliable sources, historical chronology, image attribution, readability, visual consistency, and the distinction between confirmed discoveries and scientific interpretations. We also made sure that the Phoenix lander’s findings remain separate from Opportunity’s own mission history.

SPACE RELICS is more than a presentation about a Mars rover. It is a journey through space exploration, scientific discovery, and the remarkable legacy of the machines that help humanity understand our universe.
